description: Nebulous Drift is an all-female Arab team passionate about space, programming, and data analysis. Our project processes NASA's astronomical and atomic data to map optimal lunar infrastructure sites for energy and fuel stations, turning complex science into an interactive exploration story
summary:
Project Name: Nebulous Vision
Team Name: Nebulous Drift (A dedicated team of 4 members)
Core Mission: An interactive, web-based lunar atlas designed to help researchers and space agencies evaluate and identify safe lunar landing sites, assess surface hardness, and analyze water-ice resources using real-time NASA LRO (Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter) archival data.
Key Features & Innovations:
Crater Topography Analysis: Precise evaluation of key lunar regions and craters (such as Shackleton and Faustini) based on continuous NASA archives.
Light Curve Sonification: An innovative accessibility feature that converts space transit light curves into audible audio signals, reducing eye strain and empowering visually impaired users to "hear" space data.
Interactive Technology Stack: Built using Python and Streamlit, hosted securely on Streamlit Community Cloud for seamless public and expert access.
Future Roadmap: Expanding into a comprehensive lunar simulator for future settlement, construction, and landing site modeling.
details: Team Nebulous Drift developed "Nebulous Vision" using Python and advanced computational tools, driven by a commitment to rigorous scientific accuracy and authentic data. We built our interactive platform using official NASA LRO archives to ensure reliable lunar topography, water-ice, and surface hardness analysis. Beyond visualization, our primary focus was the practical experiment: pioneering light curve sonification to convert complex space data into auditory signals, making space exploration accessible and easing eye strain, especially for visually impaired users. Every element was carefully tested and designed to deliver a true, science-backed experience.
